page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-24GB is a virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. The instance provides 8 shared vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores running on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, featuring 64 KB L1d cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI instruction sets, but lacking AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory totals 24.0 GB of RAM, resulting in an allocation ratio of 3.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated GPUs or local storage drives are bundled with this instance type, requiring external persistent volumes for disk operations, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid mid-tier computational output across multi-threaded operations alongside constrained single-core responsiveness. In stress-ng tests, the single-core score of 772.79 lands in the bottom 10 percent of recorded instances, while multi-core throughput reaches 6,254.7, aligning with middle-tier standards. Geekbench results echo this pattern with a single-core score of 1,803.0 and a multi-core score of 9,153.0. In memory metrics, small-block cached read throughput reaches 821.2 GB/sec, though uncached 256 MB reads drop to 51.42 GB/sec and writes to 36.73 GB/sec. Synthetic memory assessments show a PassMark memory score of 1,689.35, placing it in the bottom 25 percent.

Application benchmarks reflect practical performance variations across operational domains. The instance sustains 11.84 million Redis SET operations per second and handles multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 74.36 GB/sec. In contrast, static web serving throughput measures 6.02 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom quartile. CPU-based machine learning inference handles small 135M parameter models reasonably well at 110.42 text generation tokens per second, but degrades substantially on medium 7B parameter models to 5.78 tokens per second.

The shared CPU topology and absence of local storage make this instance cost-effective for general distributed computing workloads that do not demand persistent high clock speeds or continuous vector execution. Suitable workloads include containerized microservices, build pipelines, Clang-based software compilation, batch processing, and non-critical backend worker nodes. Workloads characterized by heavy single-threaded execution, high web-server bandwidth throughput, or complex local model inference are constrained by the underlying hardware profile.
